tierWhy: measurement and a retraction of my own result; no money path, no ship-gate review
headline: RETRACTION: at n=3 per arm A's five cuts show NO measurable effect. My -12.5% and my 'cut 2 carries it' were both noise at n=1.

bisectSettled.design: three arms interleaved rather than blocked (control, all-on, cut2-off, repeated three times) so drift in the deployed build or the network hits every arm equally
bisectSettled.flagsVerifiedInPage: every arm read its kill-switches back out of the page; control saw 5, cut2-off saw 1, all-on saw 0

effects.note: the sign is NEGATIVE: the arm with all five cuts active measured slightly HIGHER than the arm with all five disabled

statistics.reading: zero sits comfortably inside the interval. The instrument can only say the effect is smaller than about 6.5 MB/cycle; it cannot say it is non-zero.

bisectSettled.whatIGotWrong: W82 reported -12.5% and named cut 2 as the carrier from ONE run per arm. I flagged the risk in the same evidence — within-run spread 4.5MB against a 3.06MB effect — and the repeats landed the other way. The first-run ordering (control 24.56 > cut2off 23.29 > allon 21.50) looked like a dose-response curve and was run-to-run noise.
bisectSettled.corroboration: the PO's own series across builds is flat (b85 13.3, b99 12.8, b103 12.2), which is what a no-effect fix looks like on his instrument too. Two instruments, one conclusion.
bisectSettled.panelB: still product-retained in every b103 arm measured, anchor unchanged Window -> mainChart -> Chart._mcHostCacheFileRefOwners
bisectSettled.consequenceForCanary: all five cuts are dead weight by measurement, not just four of them. Keep the kill-switches (they cost nothing and they are what made this gradeable) but do not credit a reduction to them.

instrumentResolution.problem: a 3 MB/cycle claim is below what a 3-cycle run can resolve
instrumentResolution.numbers: per-delta sd 4.1MB; a 3-cycle run yields 2 deltas, so one run's mean carries se ~2.9MB
instrumentResolution.runsNeeded: resolving a 3 MB/cycle difference at 95% needs roughly 12 runs per arm at 3 cycles
instrumentResolution.designFix: grade on TOTAL growth over a fixed cycle count rather than a per-cycle mean (fewer, larger numbers), and treat any difference under about 5 MB/cycle as unresolvable at n=3
instrumentResolution.standingRule: no attribution from a single run per arm again, however clean the ordering looks

singleChartDoesNotLeak.agreesWithMyMechanism: retention is bound to panel-realm TEARDOWN: exactly one peer realm survives each multichart collapse, and single-chart replay never destroys a realm, so there is nothing to retain. A non-leaking single chart is what my realm-survival model predicts.
singleChartDoesNotLeak.scopeConsequence: the hunt stays on the multichart open/close path and on host caches holding panel-realm objects. No further effort on replay-side retention.

leaveOneOutDesignChange.structure: unchanged — the design already cycles multichart expand/collapse, which is the leaking operation
leaveOneOutDesignChange.sampleSize: changed, and this is the real lesson: three repeats per arm minimum, interleaved, or grade on totals
leaveOneOutDesignChange.workloadHypothesis: if replay does not leak, the replay hold may be droppable from the memory workload, which would make runs faster and less flaky (a panel-D arm hung during arming tonight)
leaveOneOutDesignChange.whyIWillNotJustDropIt: layout-only workload once under-read the leak by 34x (+0.69 vs +23.5 MB/cycle), so the workload does not get weakened without measuring which component carries the signal — indicators, order, or replay. Named as a test, not applied as an assumption.

singleChartDoesNotLeak.supportsForcedGc: his live samples swing 181MB peak to trough, roughly 40x the per-cycle signal being hunted. That is why every floor I quote follows an explicit collectGarbage, and why a per-cycle mean from live readings needs many samples.

cpuIsNotSmoothness.askedFor: state that high CPU and felt lag are separable
cpuIsNotSmoothness.whyItIsSmoothAnyway: the main thread sits at about 74.5% of a core, so roughly a quarter of it is idle, and no frame is starved. Headless was producing 124 fps (an upper bound, not vsync-capped); the same per-frame costs at 60Hz come to about 105% of a core, which brackets the PO's 111%. At 60Hz the main thread would be near 36% — abundant headroom.
cpuIsNotSmoothness.whereFeltLagWouldComeFrom: not continuous load but individual tasks exceeding the frame budget of 16.7ms. The PO's own console shows one: a 30ms forced reflow. Both of his observations are consistent — smooth overall, with occasional single tasks long enough to drop a frame.
cpuIsNotSmoothness.whatTheCpuCutsAreFor: headroom, battery and thermals, and scaling: 137% of a core for ONE panel is what makes a four-panel or fifteen-pair session saturate. They are not the smoothness fix.
cpuIsNotSmoothness.whatTheSmoothnessFixIs: eliminating the one-off long tasks — synchronous layout forced from JS — which is a different target from the per-frame continuous cost.

threeSightingsAreNotOneMechanism.askedFor: confirm the census, the shimmying order labels and the forced-reflow violation are one mechanism
threeSightingsAreNotOneMechanism.answer: NOT confirmed, and the numbers argue against it. Same class, two different sizes.

myCensus.reading: one full layout per frame, continuous, sub-millisecond

poViolation.text: [Violation] Forced reflow while executing JavaScript took 30ms
poViolation.reading: a single synchronous layout 76x the size of one per-frame layout. That drops frames; a 0.394ms layout does not.

threeSightingsAreNotOneMechanism.poShimmyingLabels: consistent with the per-frame path — order labels repositioned every frame from geometry reads
threeSightingsAreNotOneMechanism.verdict: two of the three (per-frame layout and the shimmy) are plausibly the same path. The 30ms forced reflow is a third, larger, distinct event. Calling all three one mechanism would be an argument, not a measurement.

supportingSignal.reading: stylesheet rule-sets are being invalidated 62 times a second, which is the write half of a read-after-write layout thrash and would explain both style recalc at 1.56/frame and layout at 1/frame

threeSightingsAreNotOneMechanism.measurementThatWouldSettleIt: attribute each LocalFrameView::performLayout to its PARENT trace event: nested under FunctionCall or EventDispatch means JS forced it synchronously; nested under BeginMainFrame or the lifecycle means it is scheduled. My census currently sums self time per event name and does not record parentage. That is a small addition to cpu-thread-census and it names the JS call site A has to cut.
threeSightingsAreNotOneMechanism.notRunTonight: the machine was on the bisect repeats, which the Director ranked first. Trace runs cannot share a box with memory runs without corrupting both.
